name: e2e-tier-real-io
body:
An end-to-end test exercises ONE OR MORE units WITH REAL I/O — the only tier permitted to touch the real filesystem (including temp directories), a real database (including opening a local `db.lbug`), real git, or a real spawned process. e2e may be slow; that is accepted.

e2e must still be EFFECTIVELY ISOLATED: it obeys the existing law `global.constraint.no-real-project-test` verbatim — a candidate binary is only ever exercised against a scratch /tmp git repo, never a real project, so init/scan/project/merge mutations never touch real state. The isolation rule is NOT restated or duplicated here; the e2e tier inherits it.

AC: every real-I/O test is classified e2e by definition (it crosses the `global.constraint.test-tier-boundaries` boundary); no e2e test points at a real project — it uses a scratch /tmp repo per `global.constraint.no-real-project-test`.
